title: Validation-service overrides can inject process-control environment variables into ClawPatch children
reasoning: Validation rejects only malformed names, Python import variables, and a small policy-owned set. It accepts PATH, PATHEXT, LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_* and NODE_OPTIONS, then overwrites the sanitized child environment. Repository-influenced validation-service output could therefore select an executable or load code with supervisor privileges.
reproduction: Call _release_clawpatch_env with child_env_overrides containing PATH or NODE_OPTIONS; both values are accepted and returned for child execution.
recommendation: Make process-control variables supervisor-owned. Resolve executable paths independently and reject executable-resolution, loader, runtime-hook, and shell-startup variables; preferably allow only explicitly declared service-connection variables.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were linked or included for this feature, so no visible test establishes rejection of process-control overrides.
suggestedRegressionTest: Pass PATH, PATHEXT, LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, and NODE_OPTIONS individually and assert SafetyError, while proving an allowed service variable remains accepted.
minimumFixScope: Harden _clawpatch_control_env_overrides and add focused environment-policy tests.
